properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 10 at 11:43AM CST until November 10 at 12:45PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
SMWCRP

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 1245 PM CST.

* At 1143 AM CST, a strong thunderstorm was located 51 NM east of
Port Aransas, moving northeast at 30 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas from 20 to 60 NM
and Waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from 20 to
60 NM.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.
properties.area: Waters from Baffin Bay to Port Aransas from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from 20 to 60 NM

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Devils River At Pafford Crossing near Comstock affecting Val Verde
County.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Texas...

Devils River At Cauthorn Ranch Near Juno affecting Val Verde
County.

forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Pafford Crossing nr Comstock.

* WHEN...Until late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, (1.8 meters), Moderate lowland flooding over

turbulent flow can wash motorists, campers, and equipment

Reservoir.

late this morning. It will then fall below flood stage late this
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.2
feet on 10/19/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this morning at 1100 AM CST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 10 at 9:29AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in river
levels just below Moderate flood stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady near Moderate Flood stage through this week and into
the weekend as a large volume of water works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise slightly to 3 feet late
this week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.
